dedupe_keys.name: rfc editor the rfc series of internet standards

description: The RFC Editor site is the official home of the Requests for Comments, the documents that define Internet protocols and practice. Contents: the full RFC series, including Internet Standards and historical or informative documents, a list of the latest RFCs (the page read showed RFC 10050 on JSContact profiles, RFC 10041 on advertising unreachable links in OSPF and RFC 10032 on AEGIS encryption, all from September 2026), errata, an explanation of what an RFC is and a browse and search function. Producer: the RFC Editor for the IETF, IRTF, IAB and the Independent Submissions Editor. Coverage: global protocol specifications, including the routing protocols (BGP, OSPF) that exchange points and networks rely on. Access: public web pages, one document per RFC, plus a link to the IETF datatracker for works in progress. Licence and cost: free to read; the page read states no licence. Caveats: RFCs describe protocols, not network behaviour data, and errata and later RFCs may supersede a document. Simulation uses: the protocol definitions are the reference for BGP and routing simulators that study route leaks, hijacks and cascading outages at exchange points. Related record: the YANG module collection (data-yangmodels-yang-module-collection) holding machine-readable models of network devices.
